title.raw: 卷四 文帝紀 Volume 4: Annals of Emperor Wen

sentences.zh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也，母曰薄姬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son, his mother was named Lady Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was the middle son of Emperor Gaozu, born to Lady Bo.

sentences.zh: 高祖十一年，誅陳豨，定代地，立為代王，都中都。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's eleventh year, executed Chen Xi, pacified Dai territory, established as King of Dai, capital at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after executing Chen Xi and pacifying the Dai region, he was established as King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 十七年秋，高后崩，諸呂謀為亂，欲危劉氏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year autumn, Empress Gao passed away, the Lü clan plotted rebellion, desiring to endanger the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventeenth year, Empress Gao passed away, and the Lü clan plotted rebellion in an attempt to threaten the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 丞相陳平、太尉周勃、朱虛侯劉章等共誅之，謀立代王。

translations.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and others together executed them, plotted to establish the King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang, and others joined together to execute the Lü clan and plotted to establish the King of Dai on the throne.

sentences.zh: 語在高后紀、高五王傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the Annals of Empress Gao and the Biographies of the Five Kings of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Annals of Empress Gao and the Biographies of the Five Kings of Gao.

sentences.zh: 大臣遂使人迎代王。

translations.literal: The ministers then sent people to welcome the King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then dispatched envoys to welcome the King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 郎中令張武等議，皆曰：「漢大臣皆故高帝時將，習兵事，多謀詐，其屬意非止此 也，特畏高帝、呂太后威耳。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Langzhong Zhang Wu and others discussed it, all saying: 'The Han ministers are all former generals from Emperor Gao's time, experienced in military affairs, full of cunning schemes. Their ambitions are not limited to this, they only fear the authority of Emperor Gao and Empress Lü.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Imperial Household Zhang Wu and his colleagues discussed the matter and all said: 'The Han ministers are all veteran generals from Emperor Gao's era, skilled in military affairs and full of treacherous schemes. Their ambitions extend far beyond this—they only fear the intimidating authority of Emperor Gao and Empress Lü.

sentences.zh: 今已誅諸呂，新喋血京師，以迎大王為名，實不可信。

translations.literal: Now that the Lü clan has been executed and the capital is fresh with blood, using the name of welcoming Your Majesty, it is truly not trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Lü clan has been executed and the capital still runs with fresh blood, their claim of welcoming Your Majesty is utterly untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 願稱疾無往，以觀其變。」

translations.literal: We wish you would feign illness and not go, to observe how things change.'
translations.idiomatic: We urge Your Majesty to feign illness and decline to go, so that we may observe how the situation develops.'

sentences.zh: 中尉宋昌進曰：「群臣之議皆非也。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Imperial Household Song Chang stepped forward and said: 'The ministers' discussions are all wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang, the Superintendent of the Imperial Household, stepped forward and declared: 'All the ministers' advice is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 夫秦失其政，豪 傑並起，人人自以為得之者以萬數，然卒踐天子位者，劉氏也，天下絕望，一矣。

translations.literal: When Qin lost its governance, heroic figures rose up together, those who considered themselves worthy of it numbered in the tens of thousands, yet in the end the one who ascended the imperial throne was the Liu clan. The world had lost all hope, this is the first reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin lost its grip on power, countless heroes rose up, each believing they could claim the throne—numbering in the tens of thousands. Yet in the end, it was the Liu clan who ascended the imperial throne. The world had given up all hope—that is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 高帝王子弟，地犬牙相制，所謂盤石之宗也，天下服其彊，二矣。

translations.literal: The sons and younger brothers of Emperor Gao hold territories that interlock like dog teeth, forming what is called an unshakable clan. The world submits to their strength, this is the second reason.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao's sons and brothers hold territories that interlock like jagged teeth, creating what is known as an unbreakable clan foundation. The world submits to their power—that is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 漢興，除秦煩 苛，約法令，施德惠，人人自安，難動搖，三矣。

translations.literal: Since the Han arose, it has eliminated Qin's oppressive harshness, simplified laws and commands, and bestowed benevolence and favor. Everyone feels secure, making it difficult to shake, this is the third reason.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han dynasty rose to power, it has abolished Qin's burdensome harshness, simplified the laws and regulations, and extended benevolence and favor to all. The people live in security, making the regime difficult to overthrow—that is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 夫以呂太后之嚴，立諸呂為三王，擅權專制，然而太尉以一節入北軍，一呼士皆袒左，為劉氏，畔諸呂，卒以滅 之。

translations.literal: Despite Empress Lü's severity in establishing the Lü clan as three kings, monopolizing power and ruling dictatorially, the Grand Commandant entered the Northern Army with just one tally, called out once and all the soldiers bared their left arms for the Liu clan, rebelled against the Lü clan, and ultimately destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Despite Empress Lü's iron-fisted rule in establishing three Lü kings and monopolizing power with dictatorial control, the Grand Commandant Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army with just one imperial tally. With a single command, all the soldiers bared their left arms in loyalty to the Liu clan, rebelled against the Lü faction, and ultimately destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 此乃天授，非人力也。

translations.literal: This was bestowed by Heaven, not achieved by human effort.
translations.idiomatic: This was a gift from Heaven, not something accomplished through human endeavor.

sentences.zh: 今大臣雖欲為變，百姓弗為使，其黨寧能專一邪？

translations.literal: Now even if the ministers desire to make changes, the common people will not serve as their envoys. How could their faction achieve unity?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the ministers wanted to rebel, the common people wouldn't follow their orders. How could such a faction ever unite?

sentences.zh: 內有朱虛、東牟之親，外畏吳、楚、淮南、琅邪、齊、代之彊。

translations.literal: Internally there are the close relations of Zhuxu and Dongmu, externally they fear the strength of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langya, Qi, and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court they have the support of the Zhuxu and Dongmu marquises, while externally they fear the military power of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langya, Qi, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 方今高帝子獨淮南王與 大王，大王又長，賢聖仁孝，聞於天下，故大臣因天下之心而欲迎立大王，大王勿疑也。」

translations.literal: Nowadays among Gaozu's sons only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty remain. Your Majesty is also the eldest, virtuous, sage-like, benevolent and filial, renowned throughout the world. Therefore the ministers, following the will of the world, desire to welcome and establish Your Majesty. Your Majesty should not doubt this.'
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Gaozu's surviving sons, only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty remain. You are the elder brother, renowned throughout the empire for your virtue, wisdom, benevolence, and filial piety. The ministers, following the will of the people, wish to welcome you as emperor. Do not doubt this.'

sentences.zh: 代王報太后，計猶豫未定。

translations.literal: The King of Dai reported to the Empress Dowager; his plans were hesitant and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai informed the Empress Dowager, but his plans remained uncertain and unresolved.

sentences.zh: 卜之，兆得大橫。

translations.literal: He divined it; the omen obtained was 'great horizontal.'
translations.idiomatic: He consulted the oracle, and received the omen of 'great horizontal.'

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大橫庚庚，余為天 王，夏啟以光。」

translations.literal: The interpretation said: 'Great horizontal geng geng, I become the heavenly king, Xia Qi with radiance.'
translations.idiomatic: The diviner interpreted: 'Great horizontal omen, bright and clear—I shall become the heavenly king, radiant like Xia Qi.'

sentences.zh: 代王曰：「寡人固已為王，又何王乎？」

translations.literal: The King of Dai said: 'I am already a king, what more kingship is there?'
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai replied: 'I am already a king—what greater kingship could there be?'

sentences.zh: 卜人曰：「所謂天王者，乃天子也。」

translations.literal: The diviner said: 'What is called heavenly king is precisely the Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The diviner explained: 'The heavenly king of which I speak is none other than the emperor himself.'

sentences.zh: 於是代王乃遣太后弟薄昭見太尉勃，勃等具言所以迎立王者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the King of Dai sent the Empress Dowager's younger brother Bo Zhao to see Grand Commandant Zhou Bo; Zhou Bo and the others fully explained the reasons for welcoming and establishing the king.
translations.idiomatic: At this the King of Dai dispatched Bo Zhao, the Empress Dowager's younger brother, to meet with Grand Commandant Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo and his colleagues explained in detail the reasons for welcoming and enthroning the king.

sentences.zh: 昭還 報曰：「信矣，無可疑者。」

translations.literal: Zhao returned and reported: 'It is trustworthy, there is nothing to doubt.'
translations.idiomatic: Bo Zhao returned and reported: 'It is trustworthy indeed—nothing to doubt.'

sentences.zh: 代王笑謂宋昌曰：「果如公言。」

translations.literal: The King of Dai smiled and said to Song Chang: 'Indeed as you said.'
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai smiled and told Song Chang: 'Just as you predicted.'

sentences.zh: 乃令宋昌驂乘，張武等六人乘六乘傳詣長安。

translations.literal: Then he ordered Song Chang to ride as charioteer, and Zhang Wu and five others to ride six relay carriages to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded Song Chang to serve as his chariot companion, while Zhang Wu and five others rode six relay carriages to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 至高陵止，而使宋昌先之長安觀變。

translations.literal: They stopped at Gaoling, and sent Song Chang ahead to Chang'an to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Gaoling and sent Song Chang ahead to Chang'an to assess the situation.

sentences.zh: 昌至渭橋，丞相已下皆迎。

translations.literal: When Chang arrived at Wei Bridge, the Chancellor and below all came to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Chang reached Wei Bridge, the chancellor and all the officials came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 昌還報，代王乃進至渭橋。

translations.literal: Chang returned and reported; the King of Dai then advanced to Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang returned with his report, and the King of Dai then proceeded to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 群臣拜謁稱臣，代王下拜。

translations.literal: The ministers bowed and paid respects, calling themselves subjects. The King of Dai descended and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers bowed low and acknowledged him as their sovereign. The King of Dai returned the courtesy with a bow.

sentences.zh: 太尉勃進曰：「願請間。」

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo stepped forward and said: 'I wish to request a private audience.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo stepped forward and said: 'I request a private audience.'

sentences.zh: 宋昌曰：「所言公，公言之；

translations.literal: Song Chang said: 'What you speak of as public matters, speak of them publicly;
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang replied: 'If what you wish to discuss concerns public affairs, speak of it publicly;

sentences.zh: 所言私，王者無私。」

translations.literal: What you speak of as private matters—a king has no private affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: If it concerns private matters—a sovereign has no private affairs.'

sentences.zh: 太尉勃乃跪上天子璽。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo then knelt and presented the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo then knelt and presented the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 代王謝曰：「至邸而議之。」

translations.literal: The King of Dai declined, saying: 'Let us discuss it when we reach the residence.'
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai politely declined, saying: 'Let us discuss this matter once we reach the residence.'

sentences.zh: 十二月，立趙幽王子遂為趙王，徙琅邪王澤為燕王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they established Zhao You Wang's son Sui as King of Zhao, and moved King Ze of Langya to become King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, they enthroned Sui, son of the late King You of Zhao, as King of Zhao, and transferred King Ze of Langya to become King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 呂氏所奪齊楚地皆歸之。

translations.literal: All the territories that the Lü clan had seized from Qi and Chu were returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: All territories that the Lü clan had taken from Qi and Chu were restored to their rightful owners.

sentences.zh: 盡除收帑相坐律令。

translations.literal: They completely abolished the laws on confiscating property and collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They entirely abolished the laws concerning property confiscation and collective punishment by association.

sentences.zh: 正月，有司請蚤建太子，所以尊宗廟也。

translations.literal: In the first month, the officials requested to establish the crown prince early, in order to honor the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, the officials petitioned to establish the crown prince without delay, in order to honor the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕既不德，上帝神明未歆饗也，天下人民未有轺志。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'I, being without virtue, have not yet caused the gods above to accept my offerings. The people of the world do not yet have settled hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict stated: 'Lacking virtue as I do, I have not yet won the acceptance of the gods above for my offerings. The people of the realm have not yet attained settled hearts.

sentences.zh: 今 縱不能博求天下賢聖有德之人而嬗天下焉，而曰豫建太子，是重吾不德也。

translations.literal: Now even if I cannot extensively seek out the worthy sages and virtuous people of the world to transfer the realm to them, yet to speak of establishing a crown prince in advance is to compound my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I cannot seek out the worthy sages and virtuous men of the world to entrust the realm to them, to speak of establishing a crown prince prematurely would only compound my lack of virtue.

sentences.zh: 謂天下何？

translations.literal: What would the world think?
translations.idiomatic: What would the people of the world think?

sentences.zh: 其安之。」

translations.literal: Leave it be.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter rest.'

sentences.zh: 有司曰：「豫建太子，所以重宗廟社稷，不忘天下也。」

translations.literal: The officials said: 'Establishing the crown prince in advance honors the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and does not forget the world.'
translations.idiomatic: The officials replied: 'Establishing the crown prince in advance honors the ancestral temples and the altars of state, and shows concern for the welfare of the world.'

sentences.zh: 上曰： 「楚王，季父也，春秋高，閱天下之義理多矣，明於國家之體。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. He is advanced in age, has seen much of the world's principles and righteousness, understands the structure of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. Advanced in years and experienced in the world's moral principles, he understands the proper order of the state.

sentences.zh: 吳王於朕，兄也；

translations.literal: The King of Wu is my elder brother to me;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu is like an elder brother to me;

sentences.zh: 淮南王，弟也：皆秉德以陪朕，豈為不豫哉！

translations.literal: The King of Huainan is my younger brother: all uphold virtue to assist me, how could they not be prepared!
translations.idiomatic: The King of Huainan is like a younger brother to me. All of them uphold virtue to support me—how could they not stand ready as successors!

sentences.zh: 諸侯王宗室昆弟有功臣，多賢及有德 義者，若舉有德以陪朕之不能終，是社稷之靈，天下之福也。

translations.literal: Among the feudal kings, imperial clan brothers, and kinsmen who have rendered merit, many are worthy and virtuous. If we raise those with virtue to assist my shortcomings, this would be the blessing of the altars of state and the fortune of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Among the feudal kings and imperial clansmen who have rendered meritorious service, many are worthy and virtuous. If we select those with virtue to compensate for my deficiencies, this would be a blessing to the altars of state and bring fortune to the world.

sentences.zh: 今不選舉焉，而曰必子，人其以朕為忘賢有德者而專於子，非所以憂天下也。

translations.literal: Now if we do not select from among them and insist it must be my son, people will think I forget the worthy and virtuous and am partial to my son—this is not the way to care for the world.
translations.idiomatic: Now if we refuse to select from among them and insist it must be my own son, people will think I disregard the worthy and virtuous while favoring my own child—this is not how to show concern for the world.

sentences.zh: 朕甚不取。」

translations.literal: I strongly disagree.'
translations.idiomatic: I find this most unacceptable.'

sentences.zh: 有司固請 曰：「古者殷周有國，治安皆且千歲，有天下者莫長焉，用此道也。

translations.literal: The officials firmly petitioned, saying: 'In ancient times, Yin and Zhou possessed their states, their peace and security lasted nearly a thousand years. None who possessed the world lasted longer than this, using this way.
translations.idiomatic: The officials persisted in their petition, saying: 'In ancient times, the Yin and Zhou dynasties possessed their realms, and their peace and stability lasted nearly a thousand years. No rulers who possessed the world lasted longer than they did, and this was the method they used.

sentences.zh: 立嗣必子，所從來遠矣。

translations.literal: Establishing heirs must be sons—the tradition comes from far back.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing heirs must be one's own sons—this tradition stretches far back in time.

sentences.zh: 高帝始平天下，建諸侯，為帝者太祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first pacified the world and established the feudal lords, for emperors he became the great ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first pacified the world and established the feudal lords, he became the great ancestor for all emperors.

sentences.zh: 諸侯王列侯始受國者亦皆為其國 祖。

translations.literal: The feudal kings and marquises who first received their states also all became ancestors of their states.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal kings and marquises who first received their fiefs also all became the founding ancestors of their states.

sentences.zh: 子孫繼嗣，世世不絕，天下之大義也。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeding each other, generation after generation without end—this is the great righteousness of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons succeeding one another, generation after generation without interruption—this is the supreme moral principle of the world.

sentences.zh: 故高帝設之以撫海內。

translations.literal: Therefore Gaozu established this to pacify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Emperor Gaozu established this system to pacify the empire.

sentences.zh: 今釋宜建而更選於諸侯宗室，非高帝之志也。

translations.literal: Now to abandon what should properly be established and instead select from the feudal kings and imperial clan—this is not Gaozu's intention.
translations.idiomatic: Now to abandon what should rightfully be established and instead select from among the feudal kings and imperial clansmen—this was not Emperor Gaozu's intention.

sentences.zh: 更議不宜。

translations.literal: Further discussion is not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Further debate would be inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 子啟最長，敦厚慈仁，請建以為太子。」

translations.literal: Prince Qi is the eldest, honest, kind, and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi is the eldest son, honest and sincere, kind and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'

sentences.zh: 上乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then gave his approval.

sentences.zh: 因賜天下民當為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Therefore he granted one rank of nobility to all people in the world who were to succeed their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he granted one rank of nobility to all people throughout the empire who were designated to succeed their fathers as heirs.

sentences.zh: 封將軍薄昭為軹侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed General Bo Zhao as Marquis of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed General Bo Zhao as the Marquis of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 三月，有司請立皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month, the officials petitioned to establish the empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the officials petitioned to establish an empress.

sentences.zh: 皇太后曰：「立太子母竇氏為皇后。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: 'Establish the crown prince's mother Lady Dou as empress.'
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager declared: 'Establish Lady Dou, mother of the crown prince, as empress.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「方春和時，草木群生之物皆有以自樂，而吾百姓鰥寡孤獨窮困之人或阽於死亡，而莫之省憂。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'At this time of spring harmony, all things that grow in groups have means to enjoy themselves, yet my common people—widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, and impoverished persons—some teeter on the brink of death, and no one cares for their worries.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict stated: 'In this season of spring harmony, all living things that grow in abundance have ways to enjoy themselves, yet among my people—widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, and the impoverished—some hover on the brink of death, and no one attends to their suffering.

sentences.zh: 為 民父母將何如？

translations.literal: As parents to the people, what should we do?
translations.idiomatic: As parents to the people, how should we act?

sentences.zh: 其議所以振貸之。」

translations.literal: Let them discuss means to aid and lend to them.'
translations.idiomatic: Let them deliberate on ways to relieve and assist them.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「老者非帛不煖，非肉不飽。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The elderly cannot be warm without silk, cannot be full without meat.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared: 'The elderly cannot stay warm without silk garments, cannot be satisfied without meat.

sentences.zh: 今歲首，不時使人存問長老，又無布帛酒肉之賜，將何以佐天下子孫孝養其親？

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the year, not sending people in timely fashion to visit and inquire after the elders, and moreover having no gifts of cloth, silk, wine, or meat—what then can assist the world's sons and grandsons in their filial care of their parents?
translations.idiomatic: Now at the start of the year, if we do not send people promptly to visit and inquire after the elderly, and moreover provide no gifts of cloth, silk, wine, or meat—how then can we help the sons and grandsons of the world fulfill their filial duty to care for their parents?

sentences.zh: 今聞吏稟當 受鬻者，或以陳粟，豈稱養老之意哉！

translations.literal: Now I hear that officials providing rations to those who should receive them sometimes use old grain—how does this match the intention of caring for the elderly!
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that officials distributing rations to those who should receive them sometimes give old grain—how does this befit our intention to care for the elderly!

sentences.zh: 具為令。」

translations.literal: Make a complete command about this.'
translations.idiomatic: Issue a comprehensive decree on this matter.'

sentences.zh: 有司請令縣道，年八十已上，賜米人月一石，肉二十斤，酒五斗。

translations.literal: The officials petitioned to command the counties and prefectures that for those eighty years and above, grant each person one stone of rice per month, twenty catties of meat, and five dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The officials petitioned that the counties and prefectures be commanded to grant those aged eighty and above one stone of rice per person per month, twenty catties of meat, and five dou of wine.

sentences.zh: 其九十已上，又賜帛人二疋，絮三斤。

translations.literal: For those ninety years and above, additionally grant each person two bolts of silk and three catties of floss.
translations.idiomatic: For those aged ninety and above, additionally grant each person two bolts of silk cloth and three catties of cotton wadding.

sentences.zh: 賜物及當 稟鬻米者，長吏閱視，丞若尉致。

translations.literal: For the granting of items and the rice rations that should be provided, the senior officials shall inspect, and the assistant or lieutenant shall deliver.
translations.idiomatic: For the distribution of gifts and the rice rations that should be provided, the senior officials shall oversee the inspection, and the deputy or lieutenant shall handle the delivery.

sentences.zh: 不滿九十，嗇夫、令史致。

translations.literal: For those not reaching ninety, the superintendent of agriculture and the clerk shall deliver.
translations.idiomatic: For those under ninety years of age, the agricultural superintendent and the clerk shall handle the delivery.

sentences.zh: 二千石遣都吏循行，不稱者督之。

translations.literal: The two thousand shi officials shall send metropolitan officials to make circuits, and supervise those who do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of two thousand shi rank shall dispatch metropolitan officials to inspect the districts, and supervise those who fail to comply.

sentences.zh: 刑者及有罪耐以上，不用此令。

translations.literal: For criminals and those guilty of crimes requiring hard labor or above, do not use this command.
translations.idiomatic: This edict shall not apply to criminals or those convicted of offenses requiring hard labor or more severe punishments.

sentences.zh: 四月，齊楚地震，二十九山同日崩，大水潰出。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, there was an earthquake in Qi and Chu, twenty-nine mountains collapsed on the same day, and great waters burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, earthquakes struck Qi and Chu, causing twenty-nine mountains to collapse on the same day with floodwaters bursting forth.

sentences.zh: 六月，令郡國無來獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he commanded the commanderies and kingdoms not to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, he issued a command prohibiting the commanderies and kingdoms from presenting tribute.

sentences.zh: 施惠天下，諸侯四夷遠近驩洽。

translations.literal: He extended favor to the world, and the feudal lords and four barbarians, near and far, were harmoniously united.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed benevolence upon the empire, and the feudal lords and the four barbarian tribes, both near and far, lived in harmonious concord.

sentences.zh: 乃脩代來功。

translations.literal: He then rewarded the merits from the time in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He then recompensed the merits earned during his time as King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「方大臣誅諸呂迎朕，朕狐 疑，皆止朕，唯中尉宋昌勸朕，朕已得保宗廟。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'When the ministers executed the Lü clan and welcomed me, I was hesitant and doubtful, all tried to stop me, only Superintendent Song Chang urged me, and thus I was able to preserve the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict stated: 'When the ministers executed the Lü clan and came to welcome me, I was filled with hesitation and doubt. All tried to dissuade me, but only Superintendent Song Chang urged me forward. Thus I was able to preserve the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 已尊昌為衛將軍，其封昌為壯武侯。

translations.literal: I have already honored Chang as General of the Guard, now I enfeoff Chang as Marquis of Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: I have already honored Song Chang as General of the Guard. Now I enfeoff him as the Marquis of Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 諸從朕六人，官皆至九卿。」

translations.literal: The six people who followed me, their offices all reached the Nine Ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: The six men who accompanied me shall all be appointed to the rank of the Nine Ministers.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「列侯從高帝入蜀漢者六十八人益邑各三百 戶。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The marquises who followed Gaozu into Shu and Han, sixty-eight persons, increase their fiefs by three hundred households each.
translations.idiomatic: He further declared: 'The marquises who followed Emperor Gaozu into Shu and Han—sixty-eight men in total—shall each have their fiefs increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 吏二千石以上從高帝潁川守尊等十人食邑六百戶，淮陽守申屠嘉等十人五百戶，衛尉足等十人四百戶。」

translations.literal: Officials of two thousand shi and above who followed Gaozu: Yingchuan Governor Zun and nine others shall have food revenues of six hundred households, Huaiyang Governor Shen Tu Jia and nine others five hundred households, Guard Commander Zu and nine others four hundred households.'
translations.idiomatic: For officials of two thousand shi rank and above who followed Emperor Gaozu: Governor Zun of Yingchuan and nine others shall receive food revenues of six hundred households each; Governor Shentu Jia of Huaiyang and nine others shall receive five hundred households each; Guard Commander Zu and nine others shall receive four hundred households each.'

sentences.zh: 封淮南王舅趙兼為周陽侯，齊王舅駟鈞為靖郭侯，故常 山丞相蔡兼為樊侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the uncle of the King of Huainan Zhao Jian as Marquis of Zhouyang, the uncle of the King of Qi Si Jun as Marquis of Jingguo, and the former Chancellor of Changshan Cai Jian as Marquis of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Zhao Jian, uncle of the King of Huainan, as Marquis of Zhouyang; Si Jun, uncle of the King of Qi, as Marquis of Jingguo; and Cai Jian, former chancellor of Changshan, as Marquis of Fan.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸卯晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on the last day of the month Renzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the eleventh month, the day Renzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕聞之，天生民，為之置君以養治之。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the people, and establishes rulers for them to nourish and govern them.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict declared: 'I have heard that Heaven brings forth the people and establishes rulers to nurture and govern them.

sentences.zh: 人主不德，布政不均，則天示 之災以戒不治。

translations.literal: When rulers lack virtue and their governance is uneven, Heaven shows them disasters to warn of their misrule.
translations.idiomatic: When sovereigns lack virtue and their policies are unfair, Heaven manifests disasters to admonish their poor governance.

sentences.zh: 乃十一月晦，日有食之，適見于天，災孰大焉！

translations.literal: Thus on the last day of the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse, manifest in the heavens—what disaster could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Thus on the last day of the eleventh month, a solar eclipse occurred, clearly visible in the heavens—what calamity could be more grave!

sentences.zh: 朕獲保宗廟，以微眇之身託于士民君王之上，天下治亂，在予一人，唯二三執政猶吾股肱也。

translations.literal: I have been privileged to preserve the ancestral temples, with my insignificant person entrusted above the scholars, commoners, and kings. The order or chaos of the world rests with me alone; only the two or three chief ministers are like my arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: I have been fortunate enough to preserve the ancestral temples, with my humble person placed above scholars, commoners, and kings. The peace or turmoil of the world depends entirely on me alone; only my two or three chief ministers serve as my arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 朕下不 能治育群生，上以累三光之明，其不德大矣。

translations.literal: Below I cannot properly govern and nurture all living beings; above I burden the radiance of the three luminaries—my lack of virtue is indeed great.
translations.idiomatic: Below I have failed to properly govern and nurture all living creatures; above I have burdened the radiance of the sun, moon, and stars—my lack of virtue is truly profound.

sentences.zh: 令至，其悉思朕之過失，及知見之所不及，饨以啟告朕。

translations.literal: When this command reaches you, thoroughly consider my errors and what my knowledge and vision do not reach, and report them to me bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: When this edict reaches you, carefully reflect on my faults and what my wisdom and perception fail to encompass, and report them to me frankly and without reserve.

sentences.zh: 及舉賢良方正能直言極諫者，以匡朕之不逮。

translations.literal: And recommend worthy, upright, and straightforward men who can remonstrate forcefully, to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: And recommend virtuous, upright men who speak directly and remonstrate forcefully, to rectify my deficiencies.

sentences.zh: 因各敕以職任， 務省繇費以便民。

translations.literal: Each shall be charged with their responsibilities, diligently reducing corvée labor and expenditures to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Each shall be instructed in their duties, diligently reducing forced labor and expenditures to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 朕既不能遠德，故贳然念外人之有非，是以設備未息。

translations.literal: Since I cannot extend virtue far, I constantly worry about foreigners having grievances, which is why military preparations have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Since my virtue cannot reach far, I am constantly anxious about foreigners harboring resentments, which is why military preparations have not been relaxed.

sentences.zh: 今縱不能罷邊屯戍，又飭兵厚衛，其罷衛將軍軍。

translations.literal: Now although I cannot abolish the frontier garrisons, I can at least reduce the troops and lighten the guard. Let the Guard General's army be disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Although I cannot yet abolish the frontier garrisons and border guards, I can at least trim the troops and reduce the palace guard. Let the Guard General's army be disbanded.

sentences.zh: 太僕見馬遺財足，餘皆以給傳置。」

translations.literal: The Grand Coachman has sufficient horses and surplus funds; use the remainder to supply the relay stations.'
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Coachman has adequate horses and surplus funds; use the remainder to supply the postal relay stations.'

sentences.zh: 春正月丁亥，詔曰：「夫農，天下之本也，其開藉田，朕親率耕，以給宗廟粢盛。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Dinghai day, the edict said: 'Agriculture is the foundation of the world. Let the imperial plowing field be opened. I personally will lead the plowing to supply the ancestral temple's grain offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On the Dinghai day of the first month of spring, the imperial edict declared: 'Agriculture is the foundation of the world. Let the sacred plow land be opened. I personally will lead the plowing to provide grain offerings for the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 民謫作縣官及貸種食未入、入未備者，皆赦之。」

translations.literal: People sentenced to labor for the county offices and those who borrowed seed or food but have not repaid it, or whose repayment is incomplete—all shall be pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: People condemned to forced labor for county offices and those who borrowed seed grain or food but have not repaid it, or whose repayment is incomplete—all shall be pardoned.'

sentences.zh: 三月，有司請立皇子為諸侯王。

translations.literal: In the third month, the officials petitioned to establish imperial princes as feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the officials petitioned to enfeoff imperial princes as feudal kings.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前趙幽王幽死，朕甚憐之，已立其太子遂為趙王。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Previously King You of Zhao died in confinement. I greatly pity him and have already established his crown prince Sui as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict stated: 'Previously King You of Zhao died while imprisoned. I greatly pity him and have already enthroned his crown prince Sui as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 遂弟辟彊及齊悼惠王子朱虛侯章、東牟侯興居有功，可王。」

translations.literal: Sui's younger brother Pi Qiang, and the sons of King Dao Hui of Qi—the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and the Marquis of Dongmu Liu Xingju—have merit and may be made kings.'
translations.idiomatic: Sui's younger brother Pi Qiang, and the sons of King Dao Hui of Qi—the Marquis of Zhuxu Liu Zhang and the Marquis of Dongmu Liu Xingju—have rendered merit and may be made kings.'

sentences.zh: 乃遂立辟彊為河間王，章為城陽王，興居為濟北王。

translations.literal: Then he proceeded to establish Pi Qiang as King of Hejian, Zhang as King of Chengyang, and Xingju as King of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: He then established Pi Qiang as King of Hejian, Zhang as King of Chengyang, and Xingju as King of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 因立皇子武為代王，參為太原王，揖為梁王。

translations.literal: Consequently he established imperial son Wu as King of Dai, Shen as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, he established his imperial sons Wu as King of Dai, Shen as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔曰：「古之治天下，朝有進善之旌，誹謗之木，所以通治道而來諫者也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he issued an edict saying: 'In ancient times when governing the world, the court had the banner for advancing goodness and the wood for remonstrating criticism, which served to open up the way of governance and attract remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he issued an edict: 'In ancient times, when governing the world, the court had the banner for advancing goodness and the post for remonstrating criticism, which served to open the way of governance and attract remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 今法有誹謗訞言之罪， 是使眾臣不敢盡情，而上無由聞過失也。

translations.literal: Now the law has crimes of remonstrating criticism and secret speech, which causes the ministers to not dare to express their true feelings, and the ruler has no way to hear of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: But now the law punishes criticism and secret speech as crimes. This silences the ministers and prevents them from speaking their minds, leaving the ruler with no way to learn of his mistakes.

sentences.zh: 將何以來遠方之賢良？

translations.literal: How then to attract the worthy and good from distant regions?
translations.idiomatic: How then can we attract worthy and virtuous men from distant lands?

sentences.zh: 其除之。

translations.literal: Let them be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, let these laws be abolished.

sentences.zh: 民或祝詛上，以相約而後相謾，吏以為大逆，其有他言，吏又以為誹謗。

translations.literal: When commoners curse or bless the ruler, making agreements and then deceiving each other, officials consider it great rebellion; if they have other words, officials again consider it remonstrating criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes common people curse or pray for the ruler, making pacts among themselves and then breaking them. Officials treat this as great rebellion. If they speak any other words, officials treat it as slanderous criticism.

sentences.zh: 此細民之愚，無知 抵死，朕甚不取。

translations.literal: This is the foolishness of petty people, ignorant and facing death; I greatly do not approve.
translations.idiomatic: This is merely the foolishness of ignorant common folk, yet they face the death penalty for it. I find this utterly unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 自今以來，有犯此者勿聽治。」

translations.literal: From now on, let such offenses not be investigated or punished.'
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, let such offenses go uninvestigated and unpunished.'

sentences.zh: 九月，初與郡守為銅虎符、竹使符。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he first made copper tiger tallies and bamboo messenger tallies for the commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he first issued copper tiger tallies and bamboo messenger tallies to the commandery governors.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「農，天下之大本也，民所恃以生也，而民或不務本而事末，故生不遂。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'Agriculture is the great foundation of the world, what the people rely on for life, yet the people sometimes do not attend to the root and attend to the branches, therefore their lives are not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'Agriculture forms the great foundation of the world and is what the people depend on for their livelihood. Yet some people neglect this root and pursue peripheral occupations, leaving their lives unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 朕憂其然，故今茲親率群臣農以勸之。

translations.literal: I worry that this is so, therefore this year I personally lead the ministers in agriculture to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: I am concerned about this situation, so this year I will personally lead my ministers in farming to set an example for the people.

sentences.zh: 其賜天下民今年田租之半。」

translations.literal: Let the people of the world be granted half of this year's land tax.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, let all the people of the empire be granted remission of half their land taxes this year.'

sentences.zh: 三年冬十月丁酉晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third year, winter, tenth month, Dingyou day of the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during winter in the tenth month, on the new moon day Dingyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁卯晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Dingmao day of the new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon day Dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前日詔遣列侯之國，辭未行。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'Previously I issued an edict sending the marquises to their fiefs, but the orders have not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'I previously ordered the marquises to return to their fiefs, but the command has not been executed.

sentences.zh: 丞相朕之所重，其為遂率列侯之國。」

translations.literal: The chancellor is one whom I hold in high regard; let him therefore lead the marquises to their fiefs.'
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor is a man I greatly respect; let him therefore escort the marquises back to their fiefs.'

sentences.zh: 遂免丞相勃，遣就國。

translations.literal: Consequently he dismissed Chancellor Zhou Bo and sent him to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, he dismissed Chancellor Zhou Bo from office and sent him back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太尉潁陰侯灌嬰為丞相。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Marquis Yingyin Guan Ying became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Marquis Yingyin Guan Ying was appointed chancellor.

sentences.zh: 罷太尉官，屬丞相。

translations.literal: He abolished the office of Grand Commandant and attached its functions to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the position of Grand Commandant and transferred its responsibilities to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，城陽王章薨。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, King Zhang of Chengyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, King Zhang of Chengyang passed away.

sentences.zh: 淮南王長殺辟陽侯審食其。

translations.literal: King Chang of Huainan killed Marquis Piyang Shen Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: King Chang of Huainan assassinated Marquis Piyang Shen Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 五月，匈奴入居北地、河南為寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Xiongnu entered and settled in Beidi and Henan as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Xiongnu invaded and occupied Beidi and Henan territories as raiding forces.

sentences.zh: 上幸甘泉，遣丞相灌嬰擊匈奴，匈奴去。

translations.literal: The emperor traveled to Ganquan and dispatched Chancellor Guan Ying to attack the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor journeyed to Ganquan and sent Chancellor Guan Ying to attack the Xiongnu invaders, who then retreated.

sentences.zh: 發中尉材官屬衛將軍，軍長安。

translations.literal: He mobilized the Commandant of the Capital's skilled troops and attached them to the Guard General, stationing the army at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized the skilled troops under the Commandant of the Capital and placed them under the Guard General's command, stationing the army at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上自甘泉之高奴，因幸太原，見故群臣，皆賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor went from Ganquan to Gaonu, and then proceeded to Taiyuan, where he met with his former ministers and granted gifts to all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled from Ganquan to Gaonu, then proceeded to Taiyuan where he met his old ministers and bestowed gifts upon them all.

sentences.zh: 舉功行賞，諸民里賜牛酒。

translations.literal: He promoted meritorious service and distributed rewards; to the villages and neighborhoods of the people he granted oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He honored meritorious deeds with rewards and granted oxen and wine to the villages and neighborhoods of the common people.

sentences.zh: 復晉陽、中都民三歲租。

translations.literal: He exempted the people of Jinyang and Zhongdu from three years of taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the people of Jinyang and Zhongdu exemption from three years of land taxes.

sentences.zh: 留游太原十餘日。

translations.literal: He remained touring Taiyuan for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Taiyuan, touring the area for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 濟北王興居聞帝之代，欲自擊匈奴，乃反，發兵欲襲滎陽。

translations.literal: King Xingju of Jibei heard that the emperor was on his tour in Dai, desired to personally attack the Xiongnu, but instead rebelled, mobilizing troops to attack Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: King Xingju of Jibei learned that the emperor was on his tour in Dai territory. He wanted to lead his own campaign against the Xiongnu, but instead he rebelled and mobilized troops to attack Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 於是詔罷丞相兵，以棘蒲侯柴武為大將軍，將 四將軍十萬眾擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict dismissing the chancellor's troops, appointing Marquis Jipu Chai Wu as Grand General, commanding four generals and a force of 100,000 to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, he ordered the chancellor's troops disbanded and appointed Marquis Jipu Chai Wu as Grand General to lead four generals and 100,000 troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 祁侯繒賀為將軍，軍滎陽。

translations.literal: Marquis Qi Zong He was appointed general, stationing his army at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Qi Zong He was appointed as a general and stationed his army at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，上自太原至長安。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, the emperor returned from Taiyuan to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, the emperor returned to Chang'an from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「濟北王背德反上，詿誤吏民，為大逆。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'The King of Jibei has turned his back on virtue and rebelled against his sovereign, deceiving and misleading officials and people, committing great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'The King of Jibei has abandoned virtue and rebelled against his sovereign, deceiving and misleading officials and common people alike. This constitutes great rebellion.

sentences.zh: 濟北吏民兵未至先自定及以軍城邑降者， 皆赦之，復官爵。

translations.literal: Jibei officials, people, and soldiers who pacified themselves before the army arrived and those who surrendered cities and towns with their troops, all shall be pardoned and restored to their offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: All officials, civilians, and soldiers in Jibei who pacified their areas before imperial troops arrived, and those who surrendered cities and towns along with their garrisons, shall be pardoned and restored to their offices and noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 與王興居去來者，亦赦之。」

translations.literal: Those who went to or came from King Xingju shall also be pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Those who went to King Xingju or came from him shall also be pardoned.'

sentences.zh: 八月，虜濟北王興居，自殺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, they captured King Xingju of Jibei; he committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, King Xingju of Jibei was captured and committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 赦諸與興居反者。

translations.literal: He pardoned all those who had rebelled with Xingju.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty to all who had participated in Xingju's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 四年冬十二月，丞相灌嬰薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, twelfth month, Chancellor Guan Ying died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter in the fourth year, Chancellor Guan Ying passed away.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，復諸劉有屬籍，家無所與。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, he restored to the various Liu clan members who had registered dependents but received no land allocations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, he restored land allotments to various members of the Liu clan who had registered dependents but received no property.

sentences.zh: 賜諸侯王子邑各二千戶。

translations.literal: He granted to the sons of the feudal lords cities of 2,000 households each.
translations.idiomatic: He granted each of the feudal lords' sons a city comprising 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，封齊悼惠王子七人為列侯。

translations.literal: In autumn, ninth month, he enfeoffed seven sons of King Daohui of Qi as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, he enfeoffed seven sons of King Daohui of Qi as marquises.

sentences.zh: 絳侯周勃有罪，逮詣廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: Marquis Jiang Zhou Bo committed a crime and was arrested to be brought before the Chamberlain for Law in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jiang Zhou Bo committed a crime and was arrested for trial in the imperial prison under the Chamberlain for Law.

sentences.zh: 作顧成廟。

translations.literal: He constructed the Temple of Reverent Completion.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Temple of Reverent Completion.

sentences.zh: 五年春二月，地震。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, spring, second month, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the fifth year, there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，除盜鑄錢令。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, he abolished the prohibition on privately casting coins.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, he lifted the ban on private coin casting.

sentences.zh: 更造四銖錢。

translations.literal: He reformed the coinage by minting four-zhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the currency by issuing new four-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 六年冬十月，桃李華。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, winter, tenth month, the peach and plum trees blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the sixth year, the peach and plum trees bloomed out of season.

sentences.zh: 十一月，淮南王長謀反，廢遷蜀嚴道，死雍。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, King Chang of Huainan plotted rebellion; he was deposed and exiled to Yandao in Shu, where he died in Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, King Chang of Huainan plotted rebellion. He was deposed from his throne and exiled to Yandao in Shu, where he died in Yong.

sentences.zh: 七年冬十月，令列侯太夫人、夫人、諸侯王子及吏二千石無得擅徵捕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, winter, tenth month, he commanded that marquises' grand dowagers, dowagers, feudal lords' sons, and officials of two thousand shi rank should not be permitted to arbitrarily arrest and seize people.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the seventh year, he issued an order prohibiting marquises' grand dowagers, dowagers, feudal lords' sons, and officials of two thousand shi rank from arbitrarily arresting or seizing people.

sentences.zh: 六月癸酉，未央宮東闕罘罳災。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day Guichou, the eastern gate tower screen of Weiyang Palace suffered a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guichou in the sixth month, the carved screen of the eastern gate tower of Weiyang Palace was damaged by fire.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，封淮南厲王長子四人為列侯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, summer, he enfeoffed four sons of King Li Chang of Huainan as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the eighth year, he enfeoffed four sons of King Li Chang of Huainan as marquises.

sentences.zh: 有長星出于東方。

translations.literal: A long star appeared in the eastern sky.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared in the eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 九年春，大旱。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, spring, there was a great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the ninth year, a severe drought occurred.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，行幸甘泉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, winter, he made an imperial progress to Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the tenth year, he made an imperial visit to Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 將軍薄昭死。

translations.literal: General Bo Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: General Bo Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬十一月，行幸代。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, winter, eleventh month, he made an imperial progress to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter in the eleventh year, he made an imperial visit to Dai.

sentences.zh: 春正月，上自代還。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, the emperor returned from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, the emperor returned from Dai.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，梁王揖薨。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, King Yi of Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, King Yi of Liang passed away.

sentences.zh: 匈奴寇狄道。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu raided Didao.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu invaded Didao.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬十二月，河決東郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, winter, twelfth month, the Yellow River breached its banks in Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter in the twelfth year, the Yellow River flooded Dongjun commandery.

sentences.zh: 春正月，賜諸侯王女邑各二千戶。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, he granted to the daughters of the feudal lords cities of 2,000 households each.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, he granted each daughter of the feudal lords a city comprising 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 二月，出孝惠皇帝後宮美人，令得嫁。

translations.literal: Second month, he released the beautiful women from the harem of Emperor Hui and permitted them to marry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, he released the palace ladies from Emperor Hui's harem and allowed them to marry.

sentences.zh: 三月，除關無用傳。

translations.literal: Third month, he abolished the requirement for travel documents at the passes for those without official business.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he abolished the requirement for travel passes at the border checkpoints for unofficial travelers.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道民之路，在於務本。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'The proper path for guiding the people lies in attending to the fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'The way to guide the people lies in focusing on the fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 朕親率天下農，十年于今，而野不加辟，歲一不登，民有飢色，是從事焉尚寡，而吏未加務也。

translations.literal: I have personally led the farmers of the empire for ten years now, yet the fields have not been further opened up, harvests have repeatedly failed, and the people show signs of hunger. This shows that those engaged in agriculture are still few, and the officials have not applied themselves diligently.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years now I have personally led the empire's farmers, yet the fields remain undeveloped, harvests continue to fail, and the people show signs of starvation. This indicates that too few are engaged in farming, and officials have not been diligent in their duties.

sentences.zh: 吾詔書數下，歲勸民種樹，而功未興，是吏奉吾詔不勤，而勸民不明也。

translations.literal: My edicts have been issued repeatedly, annually urging the people to plant trees, yet no success has been achieved. This shows that officials have not diligently carried out my decrees and have not clearly encouraged the people.
translations.idiomatic: My decrees have been issued repeatedly, urging the people each year to plant trees, yet no progress has been made. This shows that officials have not diligently implemented my orders and have not clearly motivated the people.

sentences.zh: 且吾農民甚苦，而吏莫之省，將何以勸焉？

translations.literal: Moreover, my farmers suffer greatly, yet officials pay no attention to them. How then can they be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my farmers endure great hardship, yet officials take no notice of them. How then can they be motivated?

sentences.zh: 其賜農民今年租稅之半。」

translations.literal: Therefore, let the farmers be granted remission of half their land taxes this year.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, let the farmers be granted remission of half their land taxes for this year.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「孝悌，天下之大順也。

translations.literal: He further said: 'Filial piety and brotherly respect are the great harmony of the world.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: 'Filial piety and fraternal duty represent the greatest harmony in the world.

sentences.zh: 力田，為生之本也。

translations.literal: Diligent farming is the foundation of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Hard work in the fields forms the foundation of life.

sentences.zh: 三老，眾民之師也。

translations.literal: The Three Elders are the teachers of the multitude of people.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders serve as teachers for the common people.

sentences.zh: 廉吏，民之表也。

translations.literal: Incorruptible officials are the models for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials serve as exemplars for the people.

sentences.zh: 朕甚嘉此二三 大夫之行。

translations.literal: I greatly commend the conduct of these two or three gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: I greatly praise the conduct of these two or three gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 今萬家之縣，云無應令，豈實人情？

translations.literal: Now in counties of ten thousand households, it is said that there are none who respond to the command. Is this truly human nature?
translations.idiomatic: Now in counties with ten thousand households, it is claimed that no one responds to the imperial command. Can this truly reflect human nature?

sentences.zh: 是吏舉賢之道未備也。

translations.literal: This shows that the officials' method of recommending the worthy is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: This demonstrates that officials' methods for recommending worthy candidates remain incomplete.

sentences.zh: 其遣謁者勞賜三老、孝者帛人五匹，悌者、力田二匹，廉吏二百石以上率百石者三匹。

translations.literal: Therefore, dispatch attendants to reward the Three Elders and filial persons with five bolts of silk each, fraternal persons and diligent farmers with two bolts each, and incorruptible officials of two hundred shi and above and one hundred shi ranked officials with three bolts each.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, dispatch attendants to honor and reward the Three Elders and filial individuals with five bolts of silk each, fraternal individuals and diligent farmers with two bolts each, and honest officials of two hundred shi rank and above as well as one hundred shi officials with three bolts each.

sentences.zh: 及問民 所不便安，而以戶口率置三老孝悌力田常員，令各率其意以道民焉。」

translations.literal: And inquire about what inconveniences the people face, and establish regular positions for Three Elders, filial persons, fraternal persons, and diligent farmers according to the population, so that each may guide the people according to their own judgment.'
translations.idiomatic: And investigate what difficulties the people face, establishing regular positions for Three Elders, filial individuals, fraternal individuals, and diligent farmers in proportion to the population, allowing each to guide the people according to their own discretion.'

sentences.zh: 十三年春二月甲寅，詔曰：「朕親率天下農耕以供粢盛，皇后親桑以奉祭服，其具禮儀。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, spring, second month, day Jia Yin, he issued an edict saying: 'I personally lead the world's farmers in plowing to provide the sacrificial grains, and the Empress personally tends silkworms to provide the sacrificial garments. Let the proper rituals be prepared.'
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on the day Jia Yin of the second month of spring, he issued an edict: 'I personally lead the empire's farmers in plowing to provide the sacrificial grains, while the Empress herself tends silkworms to supply the ritual garments. Let the appropriate ceremonies be arranged.'

sentences.zh: 夏，除祕祝，語在郊祀志。

translations.literal: In summer, he abolished the secret prayers; the account appears in the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, he abolished the secret invocations; see the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices for details.

sentences.zh: 五月，除肉刑法，語在刑法志。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he abolished the mutilating punishments; the account appears in the Treatise on Penal Law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he abolished the punishments involving mutilation; see the Treatise on Penal Law for details.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔曰：「農，天下之本，務莫大焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he issued an edict saying: 'Agriculture is the foundation of the world; no duty is greater.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, he issued an edict: 'Agriculture forms the foundation of the world; no endeavor is more important.

sentences.zh: 今廑身從事，而有租稅之賦，是謂本末者無以異也，其於勸農之道未備。

translations.literal: Now when farmers devote themselves to this task, yet they still have the burden of rent and taxes, this is no different from confusing root and branch. This shows that the way to encourage agriculture is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Now when farmers dedicate themselves to this work, they still bear the burden of rents and taxes. This makes no distinction between root and branch, showing that methods to encourage agriculture remain inadequate.

sentences.zh: 其除田之租稅。

translations.literal: Therefore, abolish the land taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, let the land taxes be abolished.

sentences.zh: 賜天下孤寡布帛絮各有數。」

translations.literal: Grant to the orphans and widows throughout the world cloth, silk, and cotton according to their numbers.'
translations.idiomatic: Grant cloth, silk, and cotton to the orphans and widows throughout the empire in appropriate amounts.'

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，匈奴寇邊，殺北地都尉卬。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, winter, the Xiongnu raided the border and killed the Beidi Commandant Ang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the fourteenth year, the Xiongnu raided the frontier and killed Commandant Ang of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 遣三將軍軍隴西、北地、上郡，中尉周舍為衛將軍，郎中令張武為 車騎將軍，軍渭北，車千乘，騎卒十萬人。

translations.literal: He dispatched three generals to station troops in Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun; made the Commandant of the Capital Zhou She the Guard General and the Commandant of the Imperial Household Zhang Wu the Chariot and Cavalry General, stationing their army north of the Wei River with a thousand chariots and one hundred thousand cavalry troops.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched three generals to station armies in Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun commanderies. He appointed the Commandant of the Capital Zhou She as Guard General and the Commandant of the Imperial Household Zhang Wu as Chariot and Cavalry General, positioning their forces north of the Wei River with a thousand chariots and one hundred thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 上親勞軍，勒兵，申教令，賜吏卒。

translations.literal: The emperor personally reviewed the troops, drilled the soldiers, reiterated the orders, and rewarded the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inspected the troops, conducted military drills, reinforced the orders, and distributed rewards to the officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 自欲征匈奴，群臣諫，不聽。

translations.literal: He wished to personally campaign against the Xiongnu; the ministers remonstrated, but he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to lead a personal campaign against the Xiongnu. His ministers remonstrated against this, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 皇太后固要上，乃止。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager firmly restrained the emperor, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager firmly prevented the emperor from going, and so he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是以東陽侯張相如為大將軍， 建成侯董赫、內史欒布皆為將軍，擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Marquis Dongyang Zhang Xiangru as Grand General, and Marquis Jiancheng Dong He and Internal Historian Luan Bu as generals, to attack the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, he appointed Marquis Dongyang Zhang Xiangru as Grand General, and made Marquis Jiancheng Dong He and Internal Historian Luan Bu generals to attack the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 匈奴走。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu retreated.

sentences.zh: 春，詔曰：「朕獲執犧牲珪幣以事上帝宗廟，十四年于今。

translations.literal: Spring: He issued an edict saying: 'I have been privileged to hold the sacrificial animals and jade and silk to serve the Supreme Deity and ancestral temples; it has been fourteen years now.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, he issued an edict: 'I have been privileged to offer sacrificial animals and jade and silk in service to the Supreme Deity and ancestral temples for fourteen years now.

sentences.zh: 歷日彌長，以不敏不明而久撫臨天下，朕甚自 媿。

translations.literal: The passing days grow longer, yet due to my lack of wisdom and clarity I have long governed the world; I am greatly ashamed of myself.
translations.idiomatic: The days grow longer, yet because of my stupidity and lack of understanding, I have governed the world for so long. I am deeply ashamed of myself.

sentences.zh: 其廣增諸祀壇場珪幣。

translations.literal: Therefore, let the sacrificial altars and grounds be broadly increased with jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, let the sacrificial altars and grounds be extensively expanded with offerings of jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 昔先王遠施不求其報，望祀不祈其福，右賢左戚，先民後己，至明之極也。

translations.literal: In ancient times the former kings bestowed favors far and wide without seeking repayment, offered sacrifices without praying for blessings, honored the worthy and placed relatives second, put the people first and themselves last—this is the pinnacle of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, the former kings extended favors far and wide without expecting repayment, performed sacrifices without praying for personal blessings, honored the worthy while placing relatives second, and put the people's needs before their own—this represents the height of enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 今吾聞祠官祝釐，皆歸福於朕躬，不為百姓，朕甚媿之。

translations.literal: Now I hear that the sacrificial officials' prayers and blessings all direct good fortune to my person and not to the people; I am greatly ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that all the prayers and blessings from the sacrificial officials direct good fortune to me personally and not to the people. I am deeply ashamed by this.

sentences.zh: 夫以 朕之不德，而專鄉獨美其福，百姓不與焉，是重吾不德也。

translations.literal: Given my lack of virtue, to monopolize and exclusively enjoy such blessings while the people do not share in them—this compounds my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Given my lack of virtue, to monopolize and exclusively enjoy such blessings while the common people get none—this only compounds my unworthiness.

sentences.zh: 其令祠官致敬，無有所祈。」

translations.literal: Therefore, command the sacrificial officials to offer respect without making any requests.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, instruct the sacrificial officials to offer respect without making any petitions.'

sentences.zh: 十五年春，黃龍見於成紀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, spring, a yellow dragon appeared in Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifteenth year, a yellow dragon appeared in Chengji.

sentences.zh: 上乃下詔議郊祀。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict to deliberate on the suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict calling for deliberation on suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 公孫臣明服色，新垣平設五廟。

translations.literal: Gongsun Chen clarified the ritual colors, and Xin Yuanping established the five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Chen clarified the ritual vestments and colors, while Xin Yuanping established the five ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 語在郊祀志。

translations.literal: The account appears in the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: See the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices for details.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，上幸雍，始郊見五帝，赦天下，修名山大川嘗祀而絕者，有司以歲時致禮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: The emperor traveled to Yong, began the suburban sacrifices to meet the Five Emperors, granted amnesty to the world, and restored the seasonal sacrifices to famous mountains and great rivers that had been discontinued, with the officials performing the rites at the appropriate times.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the emperor traveled to Yong and began the suburban sacrifices to the Five Emperors. He granted amnesty to the entire empire and restored the seasonal sacrifices to famous mountains and great rivers that had lapsed, with officials performing the rites at the proper times.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔諸侯王公卿郡守舉賢良能直言極諫者，上親策之，傅納以言。

translations.literal: Ninth month: He commanded the feudal lords, nobles, ministers, and commandery governors to recommend worthy and good men capable of speaking directly and offering extreme remonstrance; the emperor personally examined them and accepted their words.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he commanded feudal lords, nobles, ministers, and commandery governors to recommend worthy individuals capable of speaking frankly and offering bold criticism. The emperor personally examined them and accepted their counsel.

sentences.zh: 語在晁錯傳。

translations.literal: The account appears in the Biography of Chao Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: See the Biography of Chao Cuo for details.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏四月，上郊祀五帝于渭陽。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, summer, fourth month, the emperor performed suburban sacrifices to the Five Emperors at Wei Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the sixteenth year, the emperor performed suburban sacrifices to the Five Emperors at Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，立齊悼惠王子六人、淮南厲王子三人皆為王。

translations.literal: Fifth month: He enfeoffed six sons of King Daohui of Qi and three sons of King Li of Huainan, all as kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he enfeoffed six sons of King Daohui of Qi and three sons of King Li of Huainan, making them all kings.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，得玉杯，刻曰「人主延壽」。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: A jade cup was obtained, inscribed with 'The ruler's longevity extended.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, a jade cup was discovered, engraved with the words 'Long life to the ruler.'

sentences.zh: 令天下大酺，明年改元。

translations.literal: He commanded a great festival throughout the world, and changed the reign title for the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a great celebration throughout the empire and changed the reign title for the following year.

sentences.zh: 後元年冬十月，新垣平詐覺，謀反，夷三族。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Later period, winter, tenth month, Xin Yuanping's deception was discovered; he plotted rebellion and his three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of the Later reign, Xin Yuanping's fraud was exposed. He had plotted rebellion, and his three clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 春三月，孝惠皇后張氏薨。

translations.literal: Spring, third month: Empress Xiaohui Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, Empress Xiaohui Zhang passed away.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「間者數年比不登，又有水旱疾疫之災，朕甚憂之。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'In recent years the harvests have repeatedly failed, and there have been disasters of floods, droughts, and epidemics; I am greatly worried about this.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'In recent years, harvests have failed repeatedly, accompanied by disasters of floods, droughts, and epidemics. I am deeply concerned about this.

sentences.zh: 愚而不明，未達其咎。

translations.literal: I am foolish and unenlightened, unable to comprehend the cause of these faults.
translations.idiomatic: I am stupid and unenlightened, unable to grasp the source of these misfortunes.

sentences.zh: 意者朕之政有所失而行 有過與？

translations.literal: Could it be that my governance has errors and my conduct has faults?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that my administration has shortcomings and my behavior has errors?

sentences.zh: 乃天道有不順，地利或不得，人事多失和，鬼神廢不享與？

translations.literal: Or that the way of Heaven is not harmonious, earthly benefits are not obtained, human affairs are largely discordant, and the spirits are neglected and not sacrificed to?
translations.idiomatic: Or could it be that the celestial order is out of balance, earthly resources are not properly utilized, human affairs are largely in disharmony, and the spirits are neglected without proper sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 何以致此？

translations.literal: How has this come about?
translations.idiomatic: How did this situation arise?

sentences.zh: 將百官之奉養或費，無用之事或多與？

translations.literal: Could it be that the salaries of the hundred officials are too extravagant, or that useless matters are too numerous?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that the stipends of the hundred officials are too lavish, or that unnecessary activities are too abundant?

sentences.zh: 何其民食之寡乏也！

translations.literal: How scanty and lacking is the people's food!
translations.idiomatic: How meager and insufficient is the people's sustenance!

sentences.zh: 夫度田非益寡，而計民未 加益，以口量地，其於古猶有餘，而食之甚不足者，其咎安在？

translations.literal: The surveyed fields are not fewer, and the counted people have not increased. Measured by population against land, compared to ancient times there is still surplus, yet food is greatly insufficient. Where lies the fault?
translations.idiomatic: The surveyed fields are not diminished, and the population count has not grown. When measuring land against mouths to feed, compared to ancient times there is still surplus, yet food supplies are gravely inadequate. Where does the blame lie?

sentences.zh: 無乃百姓之從事於末以害農者蕃，為酒醪以靡穀者多，六畜之食焉者眾與？

translations.literal: Could it be that the common people engaged in secondary occupations that harm agriculture are numerous, those who make wine that wastes grain are many, and livestock that consume grain are abundant?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that many common people are engaged in secondary occupations that harm farming, numerous individuals are brewing wine that squanders grain, and livestock that consume grain are plentiful?

sentences.zh: 細大之義，吾未能得其 中。

translations.literal: The principles of great and small matters, I have not yet achieved their proper balance.
translations.idiomatic: The principles governing great and small matters—I have not yet found their proper middle ground.

sentences.zh: 其與丞相列侯吏二千石博士議之，有可以佐百姓者，率意遠思，無有所隱。」

translations.literal: Therefore, discuss this with the chancellor, marquises, officials of two thousand shi rank, and the erudits. If there is anything that can assist the people, think freely and deeply, without concealing anything.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, deliberate on this with the chancellor, marquises, officials of two thousand shi rank, and the erudits. If there is anything that can help the common people, think freely and reflect deeply without holding anything back.'

sentences.zh: 二年夏，行幸雍棫陽宮。

translations.literal: In the second year, summer, he made an imperial progress to the Queyang Palace in Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the second year, he made an imperial visit to the Queyang Palace in Yong.

sentences.zh: 六月，代王參薨。

translations.literal: Sixth month: King Shen of Dai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, King Shen of Dai passed away.

sentences.zh: 匈奴和親。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu made peace and became relatives by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu established peaceful relations through marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕既不明，不能遠德，使方外之國或不寧息。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying: 'I being unenlightened and unable to extend virtue far, have caused the countries beyond our borders to sometimes not have peace and rest.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: 'I, being unenlightened and unable to extend virtue to distant lands, have caused the countries beyond our frontiers to sometimes lack peace and tranquility.

sentences.zh: 夫四荒之外不安其 生，封圻之內勤勞不處，二者之咎，皆自於朕之德薄而不能達遠也。

translations.literal: Those beyond the four wildernesses do not have security in their lives, within the borders there is toil without rest. The fault in both cases comes from my thin virtue and inability to reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the four wildernesses, people lack security in their lives; within the borders, there is constant toil without respite. The blame for both situations stems from my inadequate virtue and inability to extend my influence far.

sentences.zh: 間者累年，匈奴並暴邊境，多殺吏民，邊臣兵吏入不能諭其內志，以重吾不德。

translations.literal: In recent years, the Xiongnu have repeatedly ravaged the border regions, killing many officials and people. The border officials and military officers have not been able to make clear my inner intentions, thereby compounding my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, the Xiongnu have repeatedly assaulted the border regions, killing many officials and civilians. The border officials and military officers have failed to communicate my inner intentions clearly, thereby aggravating my lack of virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫久結難連兵， 中外之國將何以自寧？

translations.literal: With long-standing enmity and continuous warfare, how can the inner and outer states achieve peace?
translations.idiomatic: With long-standing enmity and continuous warfare, how can the empire within and the states beyond achieve peace?

sentences.zh: 今朕夙興夜寐，勤勞天下，憂苦萬民，為之惻怛不安，未嘗一日忘於心，故遣使者冠蓋相望，結徹於道，以諭朕志於單于。

translations.literal: Now I rise early and retire late, laboring diligently for the world, worrying and suffering for the myriad people, feeling compassion and unease for them, never forgetting it for a single day. Therefore I have dispatched envoys with their ceremonial canopies in constant succession, crowding the roads, to make clear my intentions to the Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Now I rise at dawn and retire at night, laboring diligently for the empire, worrying and suffering on behalf of the myriad people, feeling compassion and unrest for them, never forgetting it for even a single day. Therefore I have sent envoys with their ceremonial umbrellas in constant succession, filling the roads, to communicate my intentions clearly to the Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 今單于反古之道， 計社稷之安，便萬民之利，新與朕俱棄細過，偕之大道，結兄弟之義，以全天下元元之民。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu has returned to the ancient way, considering the security of the altars of state and the benefit of the myriad people. Together with me he abandons minor grievances and follows the great way, forming brotherly relations to preserve the common people of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu has returned to the ancient way, considering the security of the state and the benefit of the myriad people. Together with me he sets aside minor grievances and follows the great path, forming brotherly bonds to preserve the common people of the entire world.

sentences.zh: 和親以定，始于今年。」

translations.literal: Peace and kinship are established, beginning this year.'
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful relations through marriage are established, beginning this year.'

sentences.zh: 三年春二月，行幸代。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, second month, he made an imperial progress to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the third year, he made an imperial visit to Dai.
