sentences.zh: 四年夏四月丙寅晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, summer, fourth month, Bingyin day of the new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the fourth year, on the new moon day Bingyin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五月，赦天下。

translations.literal: Fifth month: He granted amnesty to the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he granted general amnesty throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 免官奴婢為庶人。

translations.literal: He freed the government slaves to become commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He manumitted the government slaves, allowing them to become free commoners.

sentences.zh: 行幸雍。

translations.literal: He made an imperial progress to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He made an imperial visit to Yong.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，行幸隴西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, spring, first month, he made an imperial progress to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the fifth year, he made an imperial visit to Longxi.

sentences.zh: 三月，行幸雍。

translations.literal: Third month: He made an imperial progress to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he made an imperial visit to Yong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，行幸代。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: He made an imperial progress to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, he made an imperial visit to Dai.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，匈奴三萬騎入上郡，三萬騎入雲中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, winter, 30,000 Xiongnu cavalry entered Shangjun, and 30,000 cavalry entered Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the sixth year, 30,000 Xiongnu cavalry invaded Shangjun and another 30,000 entered Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 以中大夫令免為車騎將軍屯飛狐，故楚相蘇意為將軍屯句注，將軍張武屯北地，河內太守周亞夫為將軍次細柳，宗正劉禮為將軍次霸上，祝茲侯徐厲為將軍次棘門，以備胡。

translations.literal: He appointed Court Gentleman Ling Mian as Chariot and Cavalry General stationed at Feihu, former Chu Chancellor Su Yi as general stationed at Gouzhu, General Zhang Wu stationed at Beidi, Hedong Governor Zhou Yafu as general stationed at Xiliu, Imperial Kinsman Liu Li as general stationed at Bashang, and Marquis Xu Li of Zhuzi as general stationed at Jimen, to prepare against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Court Gentleman Ling Mian as Chariot and Cavalry General stationed at Feihu Pass, former Chu Chancellor Su Yi as general stationed at Gouzhu Pass, General Zhang Wu stationed at Beidi, Hedong Governor Zhou Yafu as general stationed at Xiliu, Imperial Kinsman Liu Li as general stationed at Bashang, and Marquis Xu Li of Zhuzi as general stationed at Jimen, all to defend against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大旱，蝗。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: There was a great drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, a severe drought occurred accompanied by locust swarms.

sentences.zh: 令諸侯無入貢。

translations.literal: He commanded that the feudal lords should not present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that the feudal lords should cease presenting tribute.

sentences.zh: 弛山澤。

translations.literal: He opened the mountains and marshes (for public use).
translations.idiomatic: He opened the mountain forests and marshes to public access.

sentences.zh: 減諸服御。

translations.literal: He reduced the various palace furnishings and carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He curtailed the various palace furnishings and imperial equipages.

sentences.zh: 損郎吏員。

translations.literal: He reduced the number of palace attendants and officials.
translations.idiomatic: He decreased the number of palace attendants and officials.

sentences.zh: 發倉庾以振民。

translations.literal: He opened the granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the government granaries to provide relief to the people.

sentences.zh: 民得賣爵。

translations.literal: The people were permitted to sell noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were allowed to sell their noble titles.

sentences.zh: 七年夏六月己亥，帝崩于未央宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, summer, sixth month, day Jihai, the emperor died in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jihai in the sixth month of summer in the seventh year, the emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：「朕聞之，蓋天下萬物之萌生，靡不有死。

translations.literal: His testamentary edict said: 'I have heard that all things that sprout and grow in the world, without exception, must die.
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary edict stated: 'I have heard that all living things in the world that sprout and grow, without exception, must die.

sentences.zh: 死者天地之理，物 之自然，奚可甚哀！

translations.literal: Death is the principle of Heaven and Earth, the natural course of things—how can one grieve excessively!
translations.idiomatic: Death is the natural principle of Heaven and Earth, the inevitable course of all things—why should one grieve excessively!

sentences.zh: 當今之世，咸嘉生而惡死，厚葬以破業，重服以傷生，吾甚不取。

translations.literal: In the present world, all praise life and detest death, using lavish burials to ruin families, and heavy mourning to harm life—I greatly disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: In the present age, everyone praises life and detests death, using elaborate burials to bankrupt families and heavy mourning garments to harm living people—I greatly disapprove of this.

sentences.zh: 且朕既不德，無以佐百姓；

translations.literal: Moreover, I being without virtue, have been unable to assist the people;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, lacking virtue as I do, I have been unable to aid the common people;

sentences.zh: 今崩，又使重服久臨，以罹寒暑之數，哀人父子， 傷長老之志，損其飲食，絕鬼神之祭祀，以重吾不德，謂天下何！

translations.literal: Now that I have passed away, I would cause prolonged heavy mourning to expose people to the rigors of cold and heat, grieve fathers and sons, harm the will of the elderly, diminish their food and drink, and cut off sacrifices to the spirits, thereby compounding my lack of virtue, what would the world think!
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have passed away, I would cause prolonged heavy mourning that exposes people to the hardships of cold and heat, grieves fathers and sons, harms the resolve of the elderly, diminishes their food and drink, and cuts off sacrifices to the spirits, thereby compounding my unworthiness—what would the world think!

sentences.zh: 朕獲保宗廟，以眇眇之身託于天下君王之上，二十有餘年矣。

translations.literal: I have been privileged to preserve the ancestral temples, entrusting my insignificant person above the lords and kings of the world for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: I have been privileged to preserve the ancestral temples, entrusting my insignificant person above all the lords and kings of the world for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 賴天之靈，社稷之福，方內安寧，靡 有兵革。

translations.literal: Relying on Heaven's blessing and the altars of state's fortune, within the four seas there has been peace, without any warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Heaven's blessing and the good fortune of the state, within the four seas there has been peace and tranquility, free from any warfare.

sentences.zh: 朕既不敏，常畏過行，以羞先帝之遺德；

translations.literal: I being unenlightened, have constantly feared committing errors, which would shame the legacy virtue of my ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: Being unenlightened as I am, I have constantly feared committing errors that would shame the legacy virtue of my ancestors;

sentences.zh: 惟年之久長，懼于不終。

translations.literal: Only fearing that my years would not be long enough to complete my duties.
translations.idiomatic: I only feared that my years would not be long enough to complete my duties.

sentences.zh: 今乃幸以天年得復供養于高廟，朕之不明與嘉之，其奚哀念之有！

translations.literal: Now fortunately I have reached my natural lifespan and can again serve at the High Temple; I being unenlightened rejoice in this—what is there to grieve and mourn!
translations.idiomatic: Now fortunately I have reached my natural lifespan and can again serve at the High Temple. Though unenlightened, I rejoice in this—what cause is there for grief and mourning!

sentences.zh: 其令天下吏民，令到出 臨三日，皆釋服。

translations.literal: Therefore, command all officials and people that when the order arrives, they shall mourn for three days and then remove their mourning clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, command all officials and people throughout the empire that upon receiving the order, they shall mourn for three days and then remove their mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 無禁取婦嫁女祠祀飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: Do not prohibit taking wives, marrying off daughters, performing sacrifices, drinking wine, or eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: Do not prohibit taking wives, marrying off daughters, performing sacrifices, drinking wine, or eating meat.

sentences.zh: 自當給喪事服臨者，皆無踐。

translations.literal: Those who are required to attend mourning rites and funerals, all shall not perform labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are required to attend mourning rites and funerals shall all be exempted from labor service.

sentences.zh: 姪帶無過三寸。

translations.literal: Mourning sashes shall not exceed three inches.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning sashes shall not exceed three inches in width.

sentences.zh: 無布車及兵器。

translations.literal: There shall be no cloth-draped carriages or weapons.
translations.idiomatic: There shall be no carriages draped in cloth nor any weapons.

sentences.zh: 無發民哭臨宮殿中。

translations.literal: Do not mobilize the people to wail and mourn within the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Do not mobilize the common people to wail and mourn within the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 殿中當臨者，皆以旦夕各十五舉 音，禮畢罷。

translations.literal: Those in the palace who are required to mourn shall each wail fifteen times in the morning and evening; when the rites are completed, they shall disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the palace required to mourn shall each wail fifteen times in the morning and fifteen times in the evening. When the rites are completed, they shall disperse.

sentences.zh: 非旦夕臨時，禁無得擅哭臨。

translations.literal: Except for the morning and evening mourning periods, it is forbidden to arbitrarily wail or mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Except for the designated morning and evening mourning periods, it is forbidden to arbitrarily wail or mourn.

sentences.zh: 以下，服大紅十五日，小紅十四日，纖七日，釋服。

translations.literal: For those below, wear great red mourning for fifteen days, small red mourning for fourteen days, and unlined mourning for seven days, then remove mourning clothes.
translations.idiomatic: For those of lower rank, wear heavy red mourning for fifteen days, light red mourning for fourteen days, and plain mourning for seven days, then remove mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 它不在令中者，皆以此令比類從事。

translations.literal: For other matters not included in this edict, all shall follow this edict by analogy in conducting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For other matters not specified in this edict, all shall proceed by analogy to this edict.

sentences.zh: 布告天下，使明知朕意。

translations.literal: Proclaim this throughout the world, so that my intentions are clearly known.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this throughout the empire so that my intentions are clearly understood.

sentences.zh: 霸陵山 川因其故，無有所改。

translations.literal: The mountains and rivers of Ba Mausoleum shall remain as they are, with no alterations made.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains and rivers of Ba Mausoleum shall remain in their natural state, with no changes made.

sentences.zh: 歸夫人以下至少使。」

translations.literal: Return the ladies-in-waiting and below to at least the status of envoys.'
translations.idiomatic: Return the ladies-in-waiting and those below them to at least the status of envoys.'

sentences.zh: 令中尉亞夫為車騎將軍，屬國悍為將屯將軍，郎中令張武為復土將軍，發近縣卒萬六千人，發內史卒萬五千人，臧郭穿 復土屬將軍武。

translations.literal: He commanded Superintendent of the Capital Zhou Yafu to be Chariot and Cavalry General, Protector of the Dependent States Han to be Garrison General, Palace Assistant Zhang Wu to be Restorer of Soil General, mobilizing 16,000 troops from nearby counties and 15,000 troops from the Capital District, with Zang Guo Chuang's Restorer of Soil assigned to General Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Superintendent of the Capital Zhou Yafu as Chariot and Cavalry General, Protector of Dependent States Han as Garrison General, and Palace Assistant Zhang Wu as Restorer of Soil General. He mobilized 16,000 troops from nearby counties and 15,000 from the Capital District, with Zang Guo Chuang's burial preparations assigned to General Wu.

sentences.zh: 賜諸侯王以下至孝悌力田金錢帛各有數。

translations.literal: He granted to the feudal lords and below, down to the filial, fraternal, and diligent farmers, gold, cash, and silk each according to their number.
translations.idiomatic: He granted gold, cash, and silk to the feudal lords and below, down to the filial individuals, fraternal individuals, and diligent farmers, each according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，葬霸陵。

translations.literal: On the day YisI, he was buried at Ba Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the day YisI, he was interred at Ba Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝文皇帝即位二十三年，宮室苑囿車騎服御無所增益。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne for twenty-three years, and the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, and furnishings were not increased at all.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator states: Emperor Xiaowen reigned for twenty-three years without adding to the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, or furnishings.

sentences.zh: 有不便，輒弛以利民。

translations.literal: If there was anything inconvenient, he immediately abolished it to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something proved inconvenient, he immediately abolished it for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲作露臺，召匠計 之，直百金。

translations.literal: Once he wished to build an open-air pavilion, summoned craftsmen to calculate it, and the cost was 100 jin.
translations.idiomatic: Once he considered building an open-air pavilion and summoned craftsmen to estimate the cost, which came to 100 jin.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「百金，中人十家之產也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'One hundred jin is the property of ten middle-class families.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'One hundred jin represents the combined wealth of ten middle-class families.

sentences.zh: 吾奉先帝宮室，常恐羞之，何以臺為！」

translations.literal: I maintain the palaces of my ancestors and constantly fear disgracing them—why would I need a pavilion!'
translations.idiomatic: I maintain my ancestors' palaces and constantly fear bringing shame to them—why would I need a pavilion!'

sentences.zh: 身衣弋綈，所幸慎夫人衣不曳地，帷帳無文繡，以示敦朴，為天下先。

translations.literal: He himself wore coarse silk, and the favored Lady Shen's robes did not drag on the ground; the curtains and canopies had no embroidered patterns, to demonstrate frugality and lead the world by example.
translations.idiomatic: He himself wore coarse silk garments, and his favored Lady Shen's robes did not trail on the ground. The curtains and canopies lacked embroidered patterns, demonstrating frugality and setting an example for the world.

sentences.zh: 治霸 陵，皆瓦器，不得以金銀銅錫為飾，因其山，不起墳。

translations.literal: In preparing Ba Mausoleum, all vessels were earthenware, not permitted to be decorated with gold, silver, copper, or tin; following the natural mountain contours, no artificial mound was raised.
translations.idiomatic: In preparing Ba Mausoleum, all vessels were made of earthenware and not permitted to be decorated with gold, silver, copper, or tin. Following the natural contours of the mountain, no artificial mound was constructed.

sentences.zh: 南越尉佗自立為帝，召貴佗兄弟，以德懷之，佗遂稱臣。

translations.literal: Nanyue's Wei Tuo established himself as emperor; he summoned and honored Tuo's brothers, and won Tuo over with virtue, whereupon Tuo submitted as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tuo of Nanyue proclaimed himself emperor. The emperor summoned and honored Tuo's brothers, winning Tuo over with virtuous conduct, whereupon Tuo submitted as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 與匈奴結和親，後而背約入盜，令邊備守，不發兵深 入，恐煩百姓。

translations.literal: He established peaceful marriage relations with the Xiongnu, but afterward they violated the treaty and raided; he ordered border defenses to be maintained but did not dispatch troops in deep pursuit, fearing to trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: He established peaceful marriage relations with the Xiongnu, but afterward they violated the treaty and conducted raids. He ordered border defenses to be maintained but did not dispatch troops in deep pursuit, fearing to burden the common people.

sentences.zh: 吳王詐病不朝，賜以几杖。

translations.literal: King of Wu feigned illness and did not attend court; he granted him a table and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu feigned illness and failed to attend court. The emperor granted him a table and staff as symbols of his advanced age.

sentences.zh: 群臣袁盎等諫說雖切，常假借納用焉。

translations.literal: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered remonstrances that were cutting, but he always accepted and employed them through accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered blunt remonstrances, but he always accepted and employed them through tactful accommodation.

sentences.zh: 張武等受賂金錢，覺，更加賞賜，以媿其心。

translations.literal: Zhang Wu and others accepted bribes of gold and cash; when discovered, he instead increased their rewards to shame their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wu and others accepted bribes of gold and cash. When this was discovered, the emperor instead increased their rewards to shame their consciences.

sentences.zh: 專務以德化民，是以海內殷富，興於 禮義，斷獄數百，幾致刑措。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to transforming the people through virtue, therefore within the four seas there was prosperity and wealth, flourishing in ritual and righteousness, judicial cases numbered only in the hundreds, nearly achieving the laying aside of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to transforming the people through virtue, resulting in prosperity and wealth within the four seas, flourishing observance of ritual and righteousness, judicial cases numbering only in the hundreds, nearly achieving the point where punishments could be set aside.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，仁哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how benevolent!
translations.idiomatic: Ah, what benevolence!
